title: Picking up banjo and guitar; the Yeah Man Club
summary: He moved from ukulele to banjo and then guitar, and mentions his first job at the Yeah Man before reordering his story.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Picking up a first guitar or banjo, self-taught

blocks.x: Well, now -- when did you first pick up your instrument?
I mean, did you start on banjo, or did you start on guitar? You had the ukelele, didn't you?
I had -- no -- I had the ukelele. And, then I picked up the banjo.
(laugh) Tell us a little bit about it.
As I say, this is after I had gotten married, and everything.
You came back to New York?
Oh, yeah. Came back to New York.
Did you stay with your aunt? You and your wife?
Yes. And, then -- let me see now. I was working in a club called the Yeah Man Club.
You mean this was your first job?
Yeah. Well, I knew how to play the ukelele.
And, the banjo, -- I could tune it -- you know what I mean. (laugh)
And, then -- I got a few books on banjo, on chords.
And, you know, I did that for a while. And, then -- after -- as soon as I picked up the banjo the guitar came in. (laugh)
Immediately. Right after, you know -- that was horrible. 'Now I have to go through this again'-- you know. The added -- the added string -- you know.
Well, who were you playing with at the Yeah Man?
Well, how did you get the job?
I got the job -- I think I'm going ahead of myself, I think.
I think I'm going a little ahead because --
Maybe you'd better think back to -- you got married, and you came to New York. And, what then? Is that the best way to go back to it?
Yeah. I think so. Like, after -- like, -- from the theaters.
Some of the theaters before I went back.
